Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:73: The fourth Palace is called Tit HaYaven [Miry Clay], and correspondingly the evil inclination is called "a stumbling stone." This Palace is called Chovah [Guilt] because it corresponds to the Palace of Merit; and all the guilts and iniquities of human beings - several angels of destruction gather them and bring them into this Palace. And on the day of judgment, when guilt and merit are weighed, if the scale of merit, the side of holiness, tips it, he is [deemed] holy and they judge him to life; and if the scale of guilt tips it, several of the masters of guilt seize him and say "he is ours" and rejoice over him and judge him to death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:74: Come and see: just as a person conducts himself in this world, so it is drawn down and bestowed upon him from above - if he pursues the impure side and transgressions, the spirit of impurity pursues him and assists him to become more impure, and causes him to come to graver transgressions and more crushing impurities than the previous ones; and if a person purifies himself and pursues holiness and sanctifies himself, a spirit of holiness is drawn down and bestowed upon him, purifying him and sanctifying him and clothing him in humility and fear, and bringing him to greater purity still, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Avodah Zarah, first chapter, "watchfulness leads to alacrity," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:75: In this Palace is the place of all those called "other gods," and they are the ones who entice human beings with the pleasures of this world, with adultery and lewdness; and over all these called "other gods" there is a spirit ruling over all of them, called El Nechar [Foreign God], and he entices those learning Torah, standing in the study hall, with evil thoughts and filth, saying to them, "why do you stand here, wasting your youth in the labor of study and weakening your strength - is it not better for you to rejoice in youth, with adultery and lewdness?" And when a person is enticed by him, several masters of impurity go after him to defile him in this world, and all these are called "boiling filth," who stand ready to sully a person, as I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:76: In the middle of this Palace is one spirit, named Nega [Plague], and from him another spirit spreads out, called Nega Tzara'at [Leprous Plague], and they stand ready to defile all the masters of slander more than all other defilers; the upper Nega we mentioned is appointed to curse all those tables not properly arranged on the Sabbath - they are all arrayed before him, and he curses them with severe curses that need not be elaborated here, may the Merciful One save us - just as the way of holiness is for good, so the way of impurity is for evil.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:77: In this Palace all matters hang for evil, except for the matters of children, life, and sustenance, which hang above in the other Palaces and descend into this Palace, and from there go forth accusers for evil - whether to diminish human beings, to kill them, or to diminish their sustenance - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:78: From this Palace goes forth one impure spirit, named Arira, and beneath his hand several thousand and myriad angels of destruction, and they are all called "cursers of the day" [orerei yom], and they are appointed over one who curses himself in anger, or over an oath or curse, and they bring it up above and thereby arouse the primordial serpent, Leviathan, the twisting serpent, to ascend and arouse severe curses, God forbid - and this is what Job intended when he said (Job 3:8) "let those curse it who curse the day" - these being the ones destined to arouse Leviathan, the twisting serpent - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:79: The fifth Palace is called Sheol, and correspondingly the evil inclination is called Arel [Uncircumcised], and he is the essence of the foreskin. In this Palace is one gate, and over it one appointee, named Eivah [Enmity], and he arouses strife and enmities in the world - after his name this Palace is called Eivah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:80: In this Palace is one impure spirit ruling over everything, named Shodad [Ravager], and he arouses ravaging and destruction, and crouches in the lofty mountains between rocks and cliffs. From this Palace all robbers are nourished, and from here go forth all murderers and killers who follow the "flaming, ever-turning sword" to kill everything; and when there is famine in the world, God forbid, this spirit called Shod [Ravage] pairs with another called Kafan [Famine] - this one to ravage the world's inhabitants and kill them, hence "Shod"; and this one to curse the food in their bellies so that they not be satisfied, hence "Kafan." And when there are those in Israel who do acts of kindness at the time of famine, they cause these not to rule in the world over Israel, and they rule instead over the idolatrous nations, and the side of impurity is subdued and Israel is blessed. And when, God forbid, there is no one in Israel to do an act of kindness, then, God forbid, the kelipah gains strength and one of these bestows upon the nations mentioned, drawing off all the flow of holiness - concerning this it is said (Song of Songs 1:6) "they made me keeper of the vineyards, my own vineyard I have not kept" - this refers to Israel, that all the flow descends from holiness to the other side, God forbid.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:81: Beneath these mentioned are impure spirits called Orlah [Foreskin], and they are the branches of the foreskin and the twigs of the foreskin, and over all of them one appointee, named Gezerdina, is appointed over all who do not observe the two years of orlah [the fruit of a young tree's first three years], and all who delay circumcision - this is the reason for "the bridegroom of blood" concerning Tziporah; and he is appointed over a person when he defiles his covenant, to bring him into Sheol and Avaddon to judge him there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:82: In the middle of this Palace is one spirit that lies in wait on the roads and in places to watch those who transgress the Torah, to slander them above, to bring enmity between the upper and lower worlds; and so they all stand ready to entice a person from the good way to the bad way, and afterward ascend and accuse him, thereby removing him from this world and the World to Come - there is no greater enmity than this, and therefore this Palace is called Eivah [Enmity]. This spirit is called Afra, meaning ash that produces no fruit and grows no plants, the opposite of holy ash, which produces fruit; the reason is, as already explained, that every spirit of impurity is castrated, and this is the ash of the burnt sin-offering, for it is bound up with sin, which is the twisting serpent. Further, when a person sins, this ash gains strength through the serpent, and this is included in the bitter waters that bring the curse - this is the earth of the Tabernacle that the priest would give the suspected wife [sotah] to drink, because she committed adultery and strayed after the harlot-serpent, and they give her to drink from the dust of the ground of the Tabernacle - this being the earth in the bitter waters, and this spirit rules over her and consumes her; this is the "latter waters," of guilt - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:83: The sixth Palace: this Palace is the highest of all the Palaces, like the side of holiness, for "this too, corresponding to that, God made," as I explained. This Palace has four gates, and in them four companies of impure ones, called Mavet [Death], Ra [Evil], Tzalmavet [Shadow of Death], and Ofel [Gloom]; these stand always to do evil and to accuse, and all four unite as one, just like the side of holiness; and concerning this mentioned union it is called "Beit Chaver" [House of Company/Charmer], as it is written (Proverbs 21:9) "than a contentious wife and a house of company [beit chaver]," and this is [related to] "and a charmer casts spells [chover chaver]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:84: Of this Palace it is said (ibid. 27:6) "but the kisses of an enemy are profuse" - here stand all those kisses and enticements and bodily desires of lewdness and adultery, through which a person is banished from this world and the World to Come, all those written in Proverbs (7:6), in the passage "for at the window of my house, through my lattice," etc. - all these enticements are from the side of the spirit of this Palace.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:85: Of her it is said (ibid. 11) "her feet do not stay in her house" - for she goes out to entice human beings; after she has enticed him, she gives him a taste of the cruel venom of vipers and takes his soul out with a sword, and in it are three drops - in one, his soul becomes confused and finds no place to rest; in the second, his soul is uprooted and departs; in the third, his face turns pale and his soul departs, breathless, etc. - all this to whoever is drawn after her, and this is what Scripture says (ibid. 5:4) "but her end is bitter as wormwood," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:86: In this Palace stand all those accusers who entice a person through his garments and clothes, that he groom his body and touch up his hair and wash his body and beautify his skin so that women will gaze upon him; over this matter one appointee, named Sektofa, is appointed. Within this appointee stands another appointee, named Marah [Mirror], through whom he looks at himself and beautifies himself and grooms himself and gazes in that mirror, and thereby becomes clothed in pride, arrogance, and coarseness of spirit; and then another power in the Palace, named Asirta, appointed over all dreams, to show a person an image which he will be drawn after, to destroy his soul; and this appointee arouses another appointee beneath his hand, who descends and arouses in the lower Palace, where Askarah is, and there arouses a certain female, Lilith, mother of demons; and when a person is aroused in his coarseness, the appointee Asirta, then Lilith becomes bound to him, and then, at every New Moon, that mirror we mentioned is aroused, with Lilith accompanying it, and sometimes the person is harmed by them and falls to the ground and is stricken with epilepsy and harmed - all this caused by the mirror, and according to the extent of his pride, so is his evil, harm, and impurity - this is [the meaning of] (Proverbs 7:23) "till an arrow pierces his liver," etc. - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:87: The seventh Palace: this Palace is the Palace of the dregs of wine to become drunk from it, as it is written (Genesis 9:21) "and he became drunk and uncovered himself within his tent" - these are the grapes Eve pressed, through which she caused death for her husband and for all who came after him - (Deuteronomy 32:32) "their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:88: In this Palace stand all those impure souls to bestow upon all those who defile themselves with a menstruant, and a married woman, and the like, such as mamzerim [children of forbidden unions] - called mamzer because he is from a foreign god [El zar]; and according to the nature of the transgression and the matter of the evil inclination, so the soul is drawn upon him from this Palace, and all who see them recognize them as invalid seed, a mamzer from a foreign god, and all his deeds testify against him that he is invalid.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:89: From this Palace goes forth one spirit appointed over all these souls, named Tzefoni [Northerner], with the mnemonic (Joel 2:20) "and I will remove the northern one [tzefoni] far from you"; corresponding to this Palace in Gehinnom is Eretz Tachtit [Lowest Land]. In this Palace is a thin point, close to the sefirot of the kelipot, and from it go forth all those thin spirits that roam the world, who see but are not seen, and these stand ready to perform wonders for human beings, since they do not stand within the filthy kelipot as much as others.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:90: Over these one appointee, named Nesira, is appointed, an Aramaic word meaning "cut off," the meaning being that he is separated from the impure kelipot to a greater degree; and these fly through the air and harm according to their side of impurity, [yet also] perform wonders in the world for those standing on the side of holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:91: From this Palace goes forth a mighty fire, and snow, and a strengthening wind to judge the wicked - this is what Scripture says (Psalms 68:15) "it will snow on Tzalmon."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:92: In this Palace stand four gates, open to the four directions, and these both grasp and do not grasp the side of holiness, and there the light of holiness shines - it is a place prepared for the pious among the nations of the world who did not do evil to Israel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:93: At the gate of the central Palace, outside, are three hundred gates, aligned corresponding to holiness, and these are places for the pious kings of the nations of the world who did not do evil to Israel and did not oppress them but protected them, and they have honor there for this, and the light of holiness shines for them within that gloom; concerning this it is said (Isaiah 14:18) "all the kings of the nations lie in glory, each in his own house."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:94: But if they oppressed Israel, several angels of destruction seize them and judge them three times each day, with several strange judgments; every single day they testify concerning Israel and their faith.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:95: Thus far the matter of these Palaces is contained. I have copied this from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (portion of Pekudei), and at first glance it might appear that these are Palaces corresponding to the sefirot of the kelipot mentioned in the previous Gate; but the reasonable view is that the sefirot are included within the Palaces, and the Palaces and the kelipot are all one matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:96: Corresponding to these seven are seven kinds of the evil inclination, which receives power from these seven, and therefore the evil inclination is called by seven names, and these are: Ra [Evil], Tamei [Impure], Sonei [Enemy], Even [Stone], Michshol [Stumbling Block], Arel [Uncircumcised], Tzefoni [Northerner]. Corresponding to these are seven chambers in Gehinnom, in which the sinner is judged for these seven kinds, and these are: Bor, Shachat, Dumah, Tit HaYaven, Sheol, Tzalmavet, Eretz Tachtit - and they correspond, one to the other: against purity, impurity; against fitness, invalidity; against permitted, forbidden; against merit, guilt - for "this too, corresponding to that, God made," as I explained in the previous chapters - so far, my teacher, peace be upon him, in Sefer HaPardes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:97: Further, one must fear the belief in reincarnation (which our Sages, of blessed memory, taught us, and Pythagoras agreed with them, although many disagree with this view), for it is far more bitter for the soul than the judgment of Gehinnom. My teacher, peace be upon him, writes that it is like a parable of a man who traveled with merchandise, a journey of two or three years, to a certain place, thinking he would profit from that merchandise there; upon arriving there, they told him, "all your labor was for naught and in vain, for this merchandise you carry is worth nothing in this place" - and that poor man returned crestfallen. How much pain reaches this man over the paucity of his wisdom and understanding, that he did not inquire and investigate what merchandise was fitting for that place, by which he would profit! And the moral is understood of itself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:98: Especially when a person knows that most souls in our generation are reincarnated, and have come now to repair what they did not repair at first - for if he departs the world without repairing what he came for, then all his toil and labor in this world is found to be in vain, and he must return a third and fourth time until he is repaired, and his punishment is great for not having repaired it the first time.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:99: Rashbi, peace be upon him, writes (Pinchas 213a) - his words: "Rabbi Shimon said: this person who undertakes a reincarnation of the soul and does not merit to be repaired thereby is as though he lies against the truth of the King, and I read of him this verse (Leviticus 5:22) 'or has found a lost object and lied about it and sworn falsely' - it would have been better for him, 'and lied about it,' not to have been created" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:100: Especially if his reincarnated soul was the soul of some wicked person, so that he is found building upon a rotten foundation, and he must first repair the foundation and only afterward build upon it, as is explained there further on, and the repair is through repentance and accepting sufferings upon himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:101: Concerning why the soul needs reincarnation even after it is purified in Gehinnom, my teacher, peace be upon him, answers that reincarnation is for two reasons: the first, for a deficiency in a mitzvah he did not complete, and he must return and complete it properly, and for this he is compelled to reincarnate, for Gehinnom is purification alone, but does not complete a deficiency.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:102: Further, it may be that he comes to repair and purify what Gehinnom cannot purify - for there are sins that Gehinnom purifies and sins that Gehinnom does not purify, and he is compelled to come to complete it. The parable for this is a man afflicted in his body with plagues in his limbs, and there are plagues that a physician can heal without amputating a whole limb, but rather cuts away a little of that decayed flesh until he is healed; and sometimes it happens that the whole limb must be cut off so that he not die and the plague reach the heart - then he cuts off the whole limb, and that person is found defective, missing one limb, one arm or one leg, and the like. Along these lines, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not wish that a person who blemished one limb so severely that, were he to enter Gehinnom, that whole limb would be annulled entirely and he would remain defective in the Garden of Eden - rather, he must return to the world to be repaired, and then it is possible that he will be defective according to the limb he first blemished, and then, at his death, he must do repentance, and thereby he repairs what happened in the previous incarnation. However, Gehinnom is only for purifying sins whose purification does not require the severing of a limb, and this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Eruvin 19a): "the transgressors of Israel - the fire of Gehinnom has no power over them, by an argument from minor to major, from the golden altar" - and this is the matter of "power" that would rule over them entirely to consume them, but rather it purifies from the outside the darkness and that blemish in the limbs of the soul, like the parable of a physician who applies a medicine to the wound to eat away that bad flesh; and when the soul leaves Gehinnom it is lacking the flesh of its limbs, as in the parable we gave, and its deficiency is completed through the light of the sun of righteousness and healing in its wings, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:103: Concerning the judgment of reincarnation, it is explained in the Sabba, portion of Mishpatim (Zohar 99b), and I shall quote a little of his words to arouse the heart - his words: "'if he takes another for himself' (Exodus 21:10) - how many great and lofty reincarnations are hinted at in this verse, for all souls enter into reincarnation, and human beings do not know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and how the scale stands, and how human beings are judged every day and every moment, and how souls enter into judgment before they come into this world, and how they enter into judgment after they leave this world - how many reincarnations and how many hidden deeds the Holy One, blessed be He, performs with naked souls, and how many naked spirits go about in that world who do not enter behind the King's curtain, and how many worlds are overturned in them, and a world overturned in several hidden wonders, and human beings do not know or take note, and how souls are tossed about like a stone in a sling, as it says (I Samuel 25:29) 'and the souls of your enemies He shall sling out from the hollow of a sling'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:104: You must know that the secret of reincarnation depends on the secret of thought, as it is written (II Samuel 14:14) "and He devises plans so that the banished one not remain banished from Him." There is also proof from the Tikkunim (100a), which says there "with Yud, reincarnation is enacted," see there. Therefore one must fear reincarnation, for there is the place of fear, as I explained in chapter 2, and it is a place where the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous even to a hair's breadth - for it says in the Tikkunim (132a), whose words we quoted in chapter 9, that any limb not properly repaired returns to come in reincarnation, even a voice or utterance not made in fear and love so that the Name be complete returns to come in reincarnation. Let every man tremble greatly over this, and be precise in his deeds, and repair his soul properly, so as not to trouble his Maker.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:105: Further, concerning the purification of the soul in the river of fire, it is explained in the Tikkunim (there, 4a) - their words: "(Ezekiel 1:1) 'and I was among the exiles by the river Chevar' - this is the river of fire that flows and issues forth from before Him, 'a thousand thousands minister to Him and ten thousand times ten thousand stand before Him,' etc. (Daniel 7:10), and souls immerse in this river of fire from the filth by which they became sullied in the lower world" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:106: My teacher, peace be upon him, explains concerning this matter, the reason why souls, after being purified in Gehinnom, still need to immerse in the river of fire, saying that there are two kinds of purification for the soul: one, in the Gehinnom on earth, is to purify what it blemished by heating itself in the fire of the inclination, to transgress the commandments; the second is to purify it for not having sanctified itself in what was permitted to it, along the lines of "sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you," such as excessive eating and other matters that will be explained in the matter of holiness, with the Lord's help - and these matters are not a complete blemish to the soul, for blemish comes only from the side of negative commandments, but rather it is the filth of this world and its desires, since this world and its desires are clothed in the skin of the serpent, and when a person does not separate from it, that filth remains acquired in his soul; and Gehinnom does not purify with physical fire except a physical blemish, namely the fire of the inclination, which is a great blemish, but this, which is not a blemish, requires a thin, spiritual fire - the supernal river of fire that flows from the Throne of Glory, of which it is written (Daniel 7:9) "His throne was flames of fire" - and through it all the physicality of this world is stripped away.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:107: There is proof for this from Rashbi (Vayakhel 211b) - his words: "and these four sources of rivers that reach the holy Throne, and from within their sweat they sweat, and from that sweat of their sweating, that river of fire is made, as it is written (Daniel 7:10) 'a river of fire flowed and issued forth from before Him, a thousand thousands minister to Him.' And souls, when they ascend, are washed in that river of fire and ascend as an offering, and they are not burned but washed. Come and see, from the salamander they make a garment, and since it is from fire, that garment is not washed except by fire - the fire consumes the filth in it and that garment is washed. So too the soul of fire, which was taken from within the Holy Throne, of which it is written 'His throne was flames of fire' - at the time it needs to be washed of that filth in it, it passes through the fire and is washed, and the fire consumes all that filth that is in the soul, and the soul is washed and refined."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:108: And if you say, if so, the soul has no punishment in this. Come and see: woe to the soul that bears a foreign fire - even though it is refined, when the filth upon it is great, woe to the soul that bears that punishment, for that filth is refined twice by fire. The first time, once it received its punishment in the body, the soul goes and they take it and bring it into a certain place called Ben Hinnom - and why is it called Ben Hinnom? Rather, there is a place in Gehinnom where souls are refined in the refining process to be purified before they enter the Garden of Eden; and if those souls are meritorious, when they bring them into that place, two angels are ready in the Garden of Eden and stand at the gate and call to those appointees in that place of Gehinnom, in order to receive that soul; and while that soul has not yet been refined by fire, those appointees call to them and say, "Hinam" [not yet]; and when it has been refined, those appointees go forth with it from that place and prepare it for the gate of the Garden of Eden, where there are those messengers, and they say to them "Hinam" [here they are] - here are the souls that have been refined - then that soul enters the Garden of Eden, and how broken it is from that breaking of the refinement of Gehinnom, which is the breaking of the lower fire that descends from above; but once it reaches the earth below, it is a fire that is not fine, and the soul is punished by it and broken. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, brings forth a sun that shines from those four gates that shine in the firmament over the Garden, and it reaches that soul and heals it - this is [the meaning of] (Malachi 3:20) 'and the sun of righteousness shall rise for you who fear My Name, with healing in its wings.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:109: The second time, after it sits in the lower Garden of Eden - all that time it sits, and until then has not entirely separated from those images and sights of this world - when they bring it up above, it must separate from all sight and all matters below, and they bring it through that river of fire; then the soul is refined by it entirely and goes forth and appears before the Master of the world, purified on all sides. Once it gazes into that light, it is healed and completed of everything; and then those souls stand in garments, crowned before their Master. Happy is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the World to Come" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:110: Here our intent in this passage is explicitly explained, in that it says, "when they bring it up above, it must separate from all sight and all matters below." And incidentally it is explained how much pain reaches the soul under the power of the fire of the lower Gehinnom, because it is physical relative to the fineness of the soul, and it is broken until the light of the supernal sun comes from the world of Atzilut; and my teacher, peace be upon him, explains that it shines from the side of Arich Anpin, in whom is all length [orech] and healing, and therefore it has the power to heal any wound that may be in the soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:111: Further, one must fear the Day of Judgment, for even Samuel was afraid of it, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Chagigah 4b): "and Samuel said to Saul, why have you disturbed me, to bring me up?" (I Samuel 28:15) - Rabbi Elazar, when he reached this verse, would weep, [saying] if Samuel the prophet was afraid of the Day of Judgment, how much more so should we be. What is this? It is written (I Samuel 28:13) "and the woman said to Saul, I see a godlike being coming up out of the earth" - "coming up" implies two: one, Samuel, and the other, that Samuel went and brought Moses with him; he said, perhaps, God forbid, I am being summoned to judgment; stand with me if there is any matter written in the Torah that I did not fulfill - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:112: Further, they say in the midrash Bereishit Rabbah (93:10): Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said, woe to us from the Day of Judgment, woe to us from the day of rebuke. Balaam, the wise man of the nations, could not withstand the rebuke of his donkey, as it is said (Numbers 22:30) "have I ever been accustomed to do so to you? And he said, no." Joseph was the youngest of the tribes, and his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed before him - when the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to rebuke each and every one according to his deeds, how much more so! As it is said (Psalms 50:21) "I will rebuke you and set it in order before your eyes."
